hook: The spring clock change raised clicks on a fake phishing email by about 13%.

readout.label: Rise in phishing link clicks after DST switch

summary: Employees at UC Irvine (N = 11,218) were randomly sent a simulated phishing email either the Monday after the switch to daylight saving time or a week earlier. The post-switch group clicked the suspicious link about 13% more often, with no change in opening or reporting the email. Sleep was not measured directly, and the study covers one workplace and one email.
title: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
